text:
Ajay: heads up — ap-sg p99 for /v1/generate spiked from ~90ms to ~420ms around 15:45 UTC, customers seeing tail latency. alerts fired.
monitor-bot: ALERT ap-sg POP latency: p99=422ms, p50=85ms, errors=0.4% — rolling 5m
Sophia: on it. checking traces + runtime logs. can someone post a sample trace id? @Kevin?
Kevin: trace 8b7f3a2 attached in tracing console. quick look: lots of kernel fallbacks to matmul_generic and attention_unfused on several hosts.
Li: that's odd — we had a model-kernel pin rollout yesterday for sg. maybe some nodes didn't get the package. verifying deployment state.
Elaine: network checks look mostly green from provider side, but I see increased retransmits on a subset of hosts (sg-3a,b,c). mtr shows asymmetric path via provider ASN 64500 -> 64600.
Sam: also seeing KV cache hitrate drop from 94% -> 61% on the same hosts, lots of cache evictions in runtime logs: "kvcache: evict shard-12 size 0.9GB" repeatedly.
Ajay: so three correlated signals: kernel fallback, kvcache thrash, and slight provider path instability. any spike in batch sizes? batching heuristics could be expanding causing kernel choice mismatch.
Sophia: looking at batching metrics: avg batch size unchanged, but bursty traffic caused many single-request microbatches at tail times. runtime decided to move to generic kernels to optimize for small sequence lengths? strange.
Kevin: pulled a profiler from sg-3b: output snippet:
```
2026-03-16T15:46:02Z profiler: top kernels by time:
 - matmul_generic 68.2%
 - attention_unfused 19.7%
 - attention_fused 0.5%
```
That explains CPU/GPU time increase.
Li: package version on sg-3b was v1.12.0-rc, while control plane rollout set recommended v1.12.1. rc lacked a heuristic fix for kernel selection when batch_size<4. oops.
Elaine: provider alarms coincide with maintenance window for peer ASN — possible slight packet reordering causing more frequent KV cache round-trip misses and eviction churn.
Sam: KV cache eviction policy uses LRU across shards; with microburst pattern and route jitter, requests land on different hosts, can't reuse local KV cache => miss storm.
Ajay: that explains it: cross-host routing jitter + some hosts running rc without kernel-selection guard = worst-case.
Sophia: quick mitigation: 1) temporarily pin routing policy to sg-pop primary for affected customers to increase sticky locality, 2) rollback nodes still on rc to recommended v1.12.1, 3) throttle batching heuristics to avoid microbatch path for short bursts.
Kevin: I can roll back sg-3b and sg-3c now (2 nodes). starting in 2m.
Li: I'll flip routing -> sticky for the next 30m for the affected shard ranges. note: this will increase load variance but should restore cache locality.
Elaine: reaching out to provider support for ASN path flap, logged ticket TN-AP-998. they confirmed a transient config push during their maintenance window.
Sam: also pushing a quick runtime patch to avoid falling back to matmul_generic when attention_fused exists — guard will prefer fused even if batch_size small; testing on canary.
Kevin: rollback done for sg-3b,c. services redeployed to v1.12.1. verifying.
Sophia: after rollback + sticky routing, p99 dropped to ~110ms within a minute. current numbers: p50=80ms p95=128ms p99=118ms. :thumbsup:
Ajay: great. still follow-ups:
 - ACTION Sophia: create postmortem with timeline + metrics + decisions (ASSIGNED)
 - ACTION Kevin: validate rollout pipeline to prevent rc nodes being marked ready without kernel heuristic patch (ASSIGNED)
 - ACTION Li: keep sticky routing on for 1h, then evaluate
 - ACTION Sam: open PR for kernel-selection guard and add unit test + perf bench (ASSIGNED)
Sophia: I'll include profiler snapshots, nvprof excerpts, and kvcache eviction logs in the postmortem. note to self: add e2e test for cross-host KV cache performance under route jitter.
Elaine: provider TN-AP-998 updated: they rolled back config; they suspect BGP session flapped for ~6 minutes. they flagged for further internal review.
Sam: next steps: consider adding server-side sticky session hints in routing to improve KV locality when backend latency crosses threshold.
Ajay: thanks everyone. I'll close the immediate incident once postmortem is created and ops runbook updated. :eyes:
Sophia: postmortem draft will be in #eng-runtime-postmortems by EOD. closing thread for now — reopen if we see regression.
